Blocks.Text: As a certified Apply with LinkedIn partner, you receive LinkedIn-verified identity and workplace information about applicants through Apply with LinkedIn with Verifications, which extends Apply with LinkedIn (AWLI). When a member verifies their identity or workplace, LinkedIn shares that result with you. Your customers (recruiters) can use verified information to prioritize applicants without leaving the applicant tracking system (ATS).

For off-site applications submitted on the customer's career site, verification data travels through the member's browser, so it is signed and bound to the member and job. For the decoded record model, refer to the Verification data schema. For AWLI, the signed wrapper is delivered in verificationData.signature. The schema below describes the validated claims inside that payload.
Note
Verification data only confirms an applicant's verified identity or workplace. It never indicates that an applicant is fraudulent, and its absence carries no negative meaning.
Apply with LinkedIn with Verifications and Apply Connect with Verifications render verification badges in the LinkedIn-hosted plugins. For more information, refer to Display verification badges.
Before you start, make sure you have:

An Apply with LinkedIn integration that is certified and approved for verification data. Work with your LinkedIn contact to request access and schedule recertification.
An Apply Connect integration that syncs jobs and screening questions.
A server-side service that can validate HS256 JSON Web Signatures (JWS) and store verification records.
A way to report application lifecycle actions to LinkedIn.
Take the following steps to add verification data to your Apply with LinkedIn integration:

Configure customer applications
Sync jobs
Deploy the Apply with LinkedIn widget
Receive and validate verification data
Report application activity
Complete certification and testing
Before implementing the widget, request access to the Apply with LinkedIn development environment and create or use the required developer applications.
If you are an ATS partner supporting multiple customers, complete these actions for every customer:

Create a customer application and store a unique client ID and client secret for that customer. The application name appears in the member consent screen.
Add the customer's fully qualified career-site domain, including protocol and any non-standard port, to the application's Valid SDK Domains setting.
Display the ATS Integration Configuration Plugin in your customer-facing configuration experience and configure it to support APPLY_WITH_LINKEDIN.
Store the integrationContext, integrationType, and tenantType that the plugin returns.
Using the customer application's OAuth 2 client credentials, enable the APPLY_WITH_LINKEDIN integration server-side and set a customer-facing integrationName.
Verify that the integration's onboarding status is ENABLED before deploying the widget.
Important
Enable customer integrations only from your server and in real time. A customer integration cannot be disabled after it is enabled.
The following plugin lets the customer request the integration. Your callback must store the returned data and send it to your server to enable the integration.

<script type="text/javascript" src="https://platform.linkedin.com/xdoor/scripts/in.js">
  api_key: {customer_client_id}
  extensions: ATSIntegrationWidget@https://platform.linkedin.com/rsc/extensions/onboarding-widget
</script>

<script type="IN/ATSIntegrationWidget"
  data-supported-bundled-integration-types="APPLY_WITH_LINKEDIN"

The detailed enablement and status-check request and error reference appears later on this page. No additional OAuth scope is required for verification sharing.
Verification data is bound to a job, not just to a customer app. If the job is not synced, LinkedIn still returns the applicant profile but omits verification data and returns JOB_NOT_SYNCED.

Set onsiteApplyOptOut to true so the job stays off-site and applicants get a single apply path.

Blocks.Text: Perform every check below when you receive the submission — not in a later batch job, since exp may have already passed by then:

Blocks.Section: Step 4: Receive and validate verification data
SectionPath: Step 4: Receive and validate verification data
Blocks.Text:
Read alg and kid from the header. Reject if alg is not HS256, or if kid does not identify one of your developer applications.
Select the application's client secret, named by kid, as the key.
Verify the HS256 signature over <header>.<payload> using a constant-time comparison.
Check that sub equals the memberIdentifier on this submission. This prevents a payload issued for one applicant from being reused for another.
Check that job equals the companyJobCode for this application, and that ver is a version you support. This prevents reuse across jobs.
Check that exp is in the future and iat is not later than the current time.
Check that jti has not been seen before. Cache processed values at least until exp.
Only now, read the verifications claim.

POST https://api.linkedin.com/v2/jobApplicationLifecycleActions

Rows.Text: This field specifies the lifecycle action, such as AWLI_APPLICATION_SUBMITTED, APPLICATION_VIEWED, RESUME_DOWNLOADED, APPLICATION_REJECTED, SCREENED, INTERVIEWED, or HIRED.

The unique job application ID on LinkedIn. For the initial AWLI_APPLICATION_SUBMITTED action, provide urn:li:jobApplication:0. LinkedIn returns a canonical urn:li:awliApplication:({memberIdentifier},{jobPostingId}) ID, composed from the member and job posting, for all subsequent actions.
The unique job posting ID within the company's system. LinkedIn uses this value to identify the job and track applications.
The encoded member ID of the applicant.
The action timestamp, in milliseconds since epoch.

Blocks.Text:
{
  "action": "AWLI_APPLICATION_SUBMITTED",
  "jobApplicationId": "urn:li:jobApplication:0",
  "partnerJobCode": "REQ-4821",
  "memberIdentifier": "VuxQHF3ULX",
  "performedAt": 1785308047000
}

For the initial AWLI_APPLICATION_SUBMITTED action, send urn:li:jobApplication:0 together with partnerJobCode and the opaque memberIdentifier returned by Apply with LinkedIn. LinkedIn doesn't need to mint a new entity to make the signal show up on Job Tracker: all it needs is the member and the job posting. LinkedIn resolves partnerJobCode to the synced job posting and returns a canonical jobApplicationId composed directly from those two IDs: urn:li:awliApplication:({memberIdentifier},{jobPostingId}). Send this same value in jobApplicationId for every subsequent action on that application.
Sample response

Authenticate with the same developer application used to sync the job. LinkedIn resolves the job posting and member from the authenticated caller and the composite jobApplicationId.
Sync the job before sending the signal. Signals for unsynced jobs are buffered and reconciled, but an unsynced job also means no verification data in the apply flow.
The write is idempotent. A repeated signal for the same member and job does not create a duplicate. Because jobApplicationId is deterministic, resending AWLI_APPLICATION_SUBMITTED for the same member and job posting returns the same value.
Store the jobApplicationId from the response and send it back unchanged in every subsequent lifecycle signal, such as SCREENED, INTERVIEWED, or HIRED, for that application.
Note
For applications that originated on your career site, LinkedIn does not send emails or notifications to the applicant. These signals are used for attribution and analytics only.

When no records are released, verificationData is present with an empty verifications list and, when available, a reason. Treat reason as optional. It discloses only partner-owned facts, so all member-specific causes collapse into one opaque value.

To ensure that other applications cannot fraudulently represent themselves as your own using the JavaScript SDK, you must configure a list of valid domains on your application that LinkedIn is allowed to trust. Ensure that you include fully qualified domain names, including the protocol (i.e. http, https) and any non-standard port numbers (other than ports 80 or 443). The way you can update/add valid domains depends on if you are a partner who provides an ATS for multiple customers or a partner who owns a proprietary ATS or career page solution.
Ensure your customers add their domains to the Valid SDK Domains field on their application's JavaScript tab:
Update the Valid SDK Domains for each customer application through the Provisioning API.
Note
Failure to allowlist JS Domain will result in an error to your browser whenever you try to load the plugin.

Deploy the Apply with LinkedIn plugin on your career site's job application page. Do not customize the AWLI button or its events with JavaScript. Use BUTTON_DATA to identify applicants and prefill profile information. Use CONVERSION to report application completion.

Rows.Text: Unique job posting id within the company's system. This value is used by LinkedIn to identify the job and for tracking purposes. If you use other integrations like RSC, PJP, AC to sync jobs to LinkedIn please ensure that this field is same as externalJobPostingId in Job Posting Schema

A value in the format of urn:li:organization:{ID}, ATS partners retrieve this after the customer has completed customer application configuration. Customers directly integrating with AWLI can refer to this help center article to find their company ID for urn:li:organization:{ID}

The mode in which this plugin will be used. Currently, the following two modes are supported:1.BUTTON_DATA Mode- Creates the Apply With LinkedIn button on the page and starts the click tracking within LinkedIn. Once applicant clicks this button and consents to sharing profile data, data is shared with partner using the callback method2.CONVERSION Mode- No visible items are created on the page. A conversion tracking event is sent back to LinkedIn to track the application status of the member. Note that the user must click the Apply With LinkedIn button on the previous page to track this conversion
The callback method handles the profile response and verificationData received after the applicant selects the plugin button. The callback is not required for CONVERSION mode.

Acceptable values are small, medium or large. The default value is medium. For reference, the size of the button is as follows:1. Small - width: 188px, height: 32px2. Medium - width: 213px, height: 48px3. Large - width: 233px, height: 48px
Acceptable values are blue, black or white. The default value is blue
